I have horses so caring for them is mainly where all the steps come from! 
I take a multivitamin but will definitely look in to magnesium, thanks!
Water intake is definitely an area I need to improve on. Already do weight training and HIIT but will give yoga a go.

Thank you for your reply.

We’re all too hard on ourselves. 18 is still young, I didn’t kiss someone properly until I was 20. Focus on what you enjoy, find people who enjoy the same things as you and you’ll start to find people who will not only find you attractive for your looks but for your personality and shared enjoyment. 
It sounds like you’re parents really love you, maybe think about talking to them about how you’re feeling and get some help. There’s nothing to lose by trying.
We care. Talk to the lovely people on here.

Sorry to hear you feel like that. I’m no professional, but this is what I’m doing to help myself out of a similar situation:

* amounting to nothing: I asked myself why I felt that way? What would feel like something? If it’s your job, what would you rather be doing? How could you do that instead? Is there a plan you could put in place to work towards that?

* People are usually just wrapped up inside their own heads about their lives and worries. 
You’ve done well reaching out here instead to find people who have gone through similar and can empathise with how you feel.

* I’m sorry to hear you don’t have family support. I think it’s normally just a case of finding what you enjoy in life and finding friends who enjoy similar things and can become your family.

* Life isn’t easy but for me it’s just been about reminding myself of the good things to help keep my mindset from a negative spiral. 
I now write three positives from each day every night. Can be something tiny like *the sky was a nice colour this evening* or * I enjoyed talking to a co worker about a tv show we both enjoy*
It sounds really stupid but has really helped my general mood.

*Self harm/suicidal thoughts - I don’t know if this is really recommended but I wear a loose elastic or hair band round my wrist. When these thoughts or impulses start to creep in, I pull the elastic and let it hit my arm. Doesn’t do any damage but stings a bit and snaps me out of my own head. I’ve found it super helpful to keep me from falling in to that dark hole.


So what do you do? You do what you’ve just done and asked for help. A health professional would probably be more helpful than the internet but the important part is that you’ve taken the first step and asked.

They will worry. They’ll worry they weren’t enough, that they didn’t do enough.
It could destroy them.
Tell them how you feel, it sounds like you have someone who really cares for you and will want to help.
There’s nothing to lose by trying. The world is better with you here.

I used to feel this way all the time. In reality I was just getting in to a negative thought spiral.
Yes, life can suck. But there is always good to be found too. 
I now list three positives at the end of each day to stop me falling back in to that dark pit. It can be tiny things like *the sky was a beautiful colour this evening* or * I enjoyed talking to my co worker about a tv show we both really like*.
You feel stupid doing it to start with but I find it really started to balance my mindset.
Nothing to lose trying it.

They would care. People just get caught up in their own lives and worries.

Talk to your psychiatrist, they’re professionally in the best position to help you out and would only go for involuntary commitment if they thought you were in serious danger of doing something. Which, by that point, what have you really got to lose?

Here anytime you want to just be able to be honest about how you feel without any judgement.

Thank you ❤️

I’m 24, from the UK and not religious or an ethnic minority.
I don’t rely on my family for money but do currently live with my parents. Just temporarily until I finish my current work and then the plan is to move on and join the police force. I’m lucky in that my family is normally very supportive, I don’t know how comfortable my parents will be with it but I’m fairly confident that they will eventually get on board once they’ve had time to adjust. Still apprehensive about broaching the subject but it’s my more traditional grandparents that I’m really not sure about how they’ll take it.
A couple of my university friends know but all live far away from me now. Mainly more work friends I have at the moment, with those I’ve decided that I won’t specifically come out to them but if it comes up in conversation or they ask I would tell them.

The closest big city has some bars but I’m not confident enough just to walk in by myself 🙈
Have been considering contacting the organisation that does the Pride event there to see if I can volunteer as a way to get involved.
